SMTO-EXE-0019 — SMTO blocked a step that clashed with an earlier one

GUID: 7a406788-87a9-4aed-b4ea-d6d1da6115af
Slug: reused-call-protocol-mismatch
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO's model sent a new step labeled the same as an earlier step but with different details. SMTO refused the new step, and the earlier step and its result are kept as they were.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Expand the task in the conversation, find the earlier step, and see whether it finished and what it changed. The earlier step may already have made its change, so doing it again could make the change twice.
  2. Watch the task for a moment; SMTO usually sends the step again as a new, separate step. The refusal goes back to SMTO's model, which can correct the clash on its own.
  3. If the task stalls, tell SMTO in the conversation what is already done and ask it to continue with the rest. This makes SMTO plan the remaining work as new steps instead of reusing the old one.

What success looks like

  • The task continues with a new step and this message doesn't come back.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; repeated clashes point to a problem with the model's replies. Don't ask SMTO to redo the earlier step until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A tool call or job identifier was reused with different arguments, direct-completion intent or stored execution fields, so the existing claim could not represent the new request and it was rejected unexecuted.

What this means

  • A call or job identifier was reused with different capability arguments, direct-completion intent or stored execution fields, so the existing claim could not represent the new request. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • A call or job identifier was reused with different capability arguments, direct-completion intent or stored execution fields, so the existing claim could not represent the new request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the original identity and request digest with the conflicting call; inspect whether the original work already ran.

How to fix it

  • Inspect and preserve the original receipt for that call_id or job_id and settle its effects; do not overwrite it. Issue any separately justified work under a new identifier; recurring collisions mean the model or client is reusing tool-call IDs.
  • Preserve and inspect the original receipt. Reconcile its effects before issuing separately authorized work under a fresh identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Original effects remain recorded and any separately justified new work has a distinct correctly correlated identity.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
